matches.meaning: Power supply fault. The unit is receiving no usable power.
The unit is restarting repeatedly, which points at a firmware crash loop.

red.primary_meaning: Power supply fault. The unit is receiving no usable power.
known_issues: Firmware 4.1.2 reboots under sustained upload above 300 Mbps.
repair_steps: Check the power adapter is pushed firmly into the round black socket at the far left of the unit, and into the wall.
Try a different wall socket that you know works.
Switch the unit off at the wall for thirty seconds, then on again.
Leave the unit powered on and connected. The firmware correction is sent to it remotely and it will restart on its own.
red.escalate_if: The power light stays red or stays off after a second wall socket has been tried.

matches.meaning: The line is up but the service is not authenticated, which usually means the account is barred.

amber.primary_meaning: The line is up but the service is not authenticated, which usually means the account is barred.
known_issues: Firmware 4.1.2 reboots under sustained upload above 300 Mbps.
repair_steps: Nothing needs to be done to the router. The line itself is working, and the service comes back on its own once the account is settled.
amber.escalate_if: The internet light is still amber more than an hour after the balance was cleared.

matches.meaning: Powered and running normally.
Fibre is connected and the line has synchronised.
The line is still synchronising. Normal for up to two minutes after a restart.

known_issues: Firmware 4.1.2 reboots under sustained upload above 300 Mbps.
repair_steps: Leave the unit powered on and wait two minutes while the line settles.
green.escalate_if: The PON light is still blinking after five minutes.

matches.meaning: No optical signal reaching the unit. Fibre is cut, unplugged, or the OLT is down.
No internet service on an otherwise live line.

off.primary_meaning: No optical signal reaching the unit. Fibre is cut, unplugged, or the OLT is down.
known_issues: Firmware 4.1.2 reboots under sustained upload above 300 Mbps.
repair_steps: Find the thin fibre lead that runs from the small box on the wall to the router.
Check both ends are pushed in fully until they click. The router end is the green PON socket, the small round socket to the left of the four yellow ones.
If the lead has come out, line the connector up with the notch facing up and press it in gently. Never force it, and never bend the fibre tightly, because it breaks.
Wait two minutes, then look at the PON light. Solid green means the line is back.
Switch the unit off at the wall for thirty seconds, then on again, and wait two minutes.
off.escalate_if: The PON light is still off after the lead has been pushed back in at both ends, or the fibre lead looks kinked, crushed or has a broken connector.

The copper line is trying to synchronise and has not settled.

known_issues: Loses DSL sync on long copper runs when line attenuation exceeds 45 dB.
repair_steps: Leave the router powered on and wait five minutes while the copper line settles.
If it is still blinking, unplug any telephone extension leads and splitters and connect the router straight to the wall socket.
green.escalate_if: The DSL light is still blinking after the router has been connected directly to the wall socket.

matches.meaning: No DSL signal at all. Cabling fault or an exchange side problem.

off.primary_meaning: No DSL signal at all. Cabling fault or an exchange side problem.
known_issues: Loses DSL sync on long copper runs when line attenuation exceeds 45 dB.
repair_steps: Find the thin telephone style cable running from the wall socket to the router.
Push it firmly into the grey DSL socket, the small square socket next to the power lead, until it clicks.
Check the wall socket end is pushed in as well, and that the cable does not run through a splitter or an extension lead.
Wait two minutes, then look at the DSL light. Solid green means the line is back.
off.escalate_if: The DSL light is still off after the cable has been pushed back in at both ends.

matches.meaning: No usable mobile signal at this location.
Power supply fault.

red.primary_meaning: No usable mobile signal at this location.
repair_steps: Move the unit next to a window, or to the highest floor of the building. The signal is much weaker inside thick walls.
Leave it in the new position for two minutes and watch the signal light.
If it is still red, switch the unit off for thirty seconds and on again so it searches for the network from scratch.
Check the power adapter is pushed firmly into the round black socket at the far left of the unit, and into the wall.
Try a different wall socket that you know works.
Switch the unit off at the wall for thirty seconds, then on again.
red.escalate_if: The signal light stays red after the unit has been moved next to a window and restarted.
